# Category tree

Only these categories may be used. An article gets exactly one field category and the Gospel themes it really explores. Write `[[Category:<name>]]` with the name for the page's wiki. The maintenance and tracking categories that SV templates add themselves (e.g. `{{SV WIP}}`, `{{SV cathopedia}}`) are the exception: they are not listed here and are never written by hand.

## en

Root: Seeds of the Word

### Fields

- Arts (`arts`): Creative practices and their works, following UNESCO's cultural domains: literature, the performing, visual and audiovisual arts, architecture, crafts, cultural heritage and gastronomy.
  - Literature (`literature`): Written and oral works of imagination and of artful prose, in any language. Studies about literature belong under Literary studies.
    - Poetry (`poetry`): Works in verse: lyric, epic, dramatic and sacred poetry, hymns and song lyrics read as poems.
    - Novels (`novels`): Book-length works of narrative prose fiction.
    - Short stories (`short-fiction`): Short narrative prose fiction: short stories, novellas, tales and fables.
    - Drama (`drama`): Plays and other dramatic works as written texts. Their staging belongs under Theatre.
    - Essays (`essays`): Non-fiction prose of literary value: essays, letters, memoirs, autobiographies, spiritual writings published as literature.
    - Children's literature (`childrens-literature`): Literature written for children and young readers, in any form.
  - Performing arts (`performing-arts`): Arts performed live before an audience: music, theatre, dance and their combined forms.
    - Music (`music`): Musical works, songs, albums and performers. Studies about music belong under Musicology.
      - Classical music (`classical-music`): Art music of the Western tradition and its concert repertoire: symphonies, chamber music, concertos, art songs.
      - Sacred music (`sacred-music`): Music for worship or on religious texts: chant, masses, oratorios, hymns, gospel and contemporary Christian music.
      - Popular music (`popular-music`): Commercial music of mass audiences: pop, rock, folk-rock, country, singer-songwriters, soundtracks released as songs.
      - Folk music (`folk-music`): Traditional music transmitted within a people or region.
    - Theatre (`theatre`): The staging and performance of plays and theatrical shows. Plays as texts belong under Drama.
    - Dance (`dance`): Dance works and forms: ballet, modern dance, folk and liturgical dance.
    - Musical theatre (`musical-theatre`): Stage musicals combining songs, spoken dialogue and dance.
    - Opera (`opera`): Staged works sung throughout with orchestra: opera, operetta, and their libretti as staged works.
  - Visual arts (`visual-arts`): Arts that produce works to be seen: painting, sculpture, drawing, printmaking, photography.
    - Painting (`painting`): Works of paint applied to a surface, by technique.
      - Fresco (`fresco`): Painting on fresh plaster, including church and palace cycles.
      - Oil painting (`oil-painting`): Painting with oil-based paints, on canvas or panel.
      - Watercolor (`watercolor`): Painting with water-soluble pigments on paper.
      - Icon painting (`icon-painting`): Painted sacred images of the Eastern and Western Christian traditions, especially icons on panel.
      - Cave painting (`cave-painting`): Prehistoric painting and engraving on rock surfaces.
    - Sculpture (`sculpture`): Three-dimensional works carved, modelled or cast, in any material.
    - Drawing (`drawing`): Works made by drawing on a surface with dry or wet media.
      - Charcoal drawing (`charcoal-drawing`): Drawings made with charcoal.
      - Pencil drawing (`pencil-drawing`): Drawings made with graphite or coloured pencils.
    - Printmaking (`printmaking`): Works printed from a matrix: engraving, etching, woodcut, lithography.
      - Engraving (`engraving`): Prints from lines cut into a plate or block.
      - Etching (`etching`): Prints from lines bitten into a metal plate by acid.
    - Photography (`photography`): Photographic works and photographers, by genre or technique.
      - Black-and-white photography (`bw-photography`): Photographs in monochrome.
      - HDR photography (`hdr-photography`): Photographs made with high-dynamic-range technique.
      - Landscape photography (`landscape-photography`): Photographs whose subject is natural or built landscape.
      - Portrait photography (`portrait-photography`): Photographs whose subject is a person or group.
    - Comics (`comics`): Sequential art telling a story in drawn panels: comic strips, comic books, graphic novels, manga.
  - Crafts and decorative arts (`crafts`): Applied and decorative arts producing crafted objects: ceramics, glass, mosaic, textiles, metalwork, calligraphy.
    - Ceramic art (`ceramics`): Pottery, porcelain and other fired-clay works.
    - Glass art (`glass-art`): Works made of or in glass.
      - Glassblowing (`glassblowing`): Objects formed by blowing molten glass.
      - Stained glass (`stained-glass`): Coloured glass windows and panels, in churches and elsewhere.
    - Mosaic (`mosaic`): Images made of small pieces of stone, glass or ceramic set in a surface.
    - Tapestry (`tapestry`): Woven textile images and other textile arts such as embroidery.
    - Goldsmithing (`goldsmithing`): Works in gold, silver and precious metals, including liturgical vessels and reliquaries.
    - Calligraphy and illumination (`calligraphy`): Artistic lettering and the decoration of manuscripts.
  - Architecture (`architecture`): Buildings and the art of designing them, by type and style. The engineering of structures belongs under Civil engineering.
    - Sacred architecture (`sacred-architecture`): Churches, cathedrals, monasteries, shrines and other places of worship.
    - Landscape architecture (`landscape-architecture`): Gardens, parks and designed landscapes.
  - Design (`design`): The design of objects and visual communication.
    - Graphic design (`graphic-design`): Visual communication by typography, images and layout.
    - Industrial design (`industrial-design`): The design of mass-produced objects.
  - Audiovisual and interactive media (`audiovisual-media`): Works made to be watched, heard or played on a screen or broadcast: film, television, radio, animation, video games.
    - Film (`film`): Motion pictures released as films, and filmmakers. Genres are not categories; they go in the infobox.
      - Feature films (`feature-films`): Fiction films of full length.
      - Short films (`short-films`): Films of short length.
      - Documentary films (`documentary-films`): Non-fiction films.
    - Television (`television`): Television series, miniseries, sitcoms and programmes. Genres are not categories.
    - Radio (`radio`): Radio programmes and dramas.
    - Animation (`animation`): Animated films and series, by any technique.
    - Video games (`video-games`): Interactive games played on a screen, and their makers.
  - Cultural heritage (`heritage`): Inherited tangible and intangible culture: monuments, traditions, festivals, folklore and symbols of peoples.
    - Monuments and historic sites (`monuments`): Historic buildings, sites and memorials as heritage.
    - Cultural traditions (`cultural-traditions`): Customs, rites and practices handed down within a culture.
    - Festivals (`festivals`): Recurring celebrations, popular feasts and festivals.
    - Folklore and mythology (`folklore`): Myths, legends, fairy tales and popular beliefs of peoples.
    - Christian roots of Europe (`christian-roots`): How Christianity shaped the culture, institutions and identity of Europe.
    - Flags and symbols (`flags`): Flags, coats of arms and other symbols of peoples, states and institutions.
  - Culinary arts (`culinary-arts`): Food, cooking, wine and the culture of the table.
- Humanities (`humanities`): The study of human culture and thought, following OECD Fields of Science group 6: history, languages and literature, philosophy, theology, the study of the arts.
  - History (`history`): The study of the human past and historical works, by period.
    - Ancient history (`ancient-history`): From the beginnings of writing to the end of Antiquity.
    - Medieval history (`medieval-history`): The Middle Ages, about 500 to 1500.
    - Modern history (`modern-history`): About 1500 to the end of the eighteenth century.
    - Contemporary history (`contemporary-history`): From the end of the eighteenth century to the present.
    - Church history (`church-history`): The history of the Church and of Christianity.
  - Archaeology (`archaeology`): The study of the human past through material remains.
  - Linguistics (`linguistics`): The scientific study of language and of particular languages.
  - Literary studies (`literary-studies`): Literary theory, criticism and the history of literature. Literary works themselves belong under Literature.
  - Philosophy (`philosophy`): Philosophical works, thinkers and disciplines.
    - Metaphysics (`metaphysics`): Being, causes, God as known by reason, the nature of reality.
    - Epistemology (`epistemology`): Knowledge, truth and certainty.
    - Ethics (`ethics`): Philosophical moral reflection: the good, virtue, duty, natural law.
      - Bioethics (`bioethics`): Ethical questions of life, medicine and biotechnology.
    - Logic (`logic`): The study of valid reasoning and argument.
    - Aesthetics (`aesthetics`): Beauty, art and taste as philosophical questions.
    - Political philosophy (`political-philosophy`): The common good, justice, authority and the state as philosophical questions.
  - Theology (`theology`): The study of God and of revelation in the light of faith, as an academic discipline. Religious life and practice belong under Religion.
    - Biblical studies (`biblical-studies`): Exegesis, interpretation and the history of the books of the Bible.
    - Dogmatic theology (`dogmatic-theology`): The doctrines of faith: Trinity, Christ, Church, sacraments, last things.
    - Moral theology (`moral-theology`): Christian moral life in the light of faith, including Catholic social teaching.
    - Patristics (`patristics`): The Fathers of the Church and their writings.
    - Spiritual theology (`spiritual-theology`): Prayer, mysticism and the spiritual life.
  - Art history (`art-history`): The study of the visual arts and architecture through history.
  - Musicology (`musicology`): The study of music, its history and theory.
  - Film studies (`film-studies`): The study and criticism of film and other audiovisual media.
- Social sciences (`social-sciences`): The study of human behaviour and society, following OECD Fields of Science group 5.
  - Psychology (`psychology`): The study of the mind and behaviour.
  - Economics (`economics`): The study of production, exchange and use of goods, and of business.
  - Education (`education`): Teaching, schooling and formation.
  - Sociology (`sociology`): Society, social groups, family and social change.
  - Anthropology (`anthropology`): Cultural and social anthropology: the comparative study of peoples and cultures.
  - Law (`law`): Legal systems, laws and jurisprudence, including canon law.
  - Political science (`political-science`): Government, politics, international relations and public policy.
  - Geography (`geography`): The study of places, peoples and their environments.
  - Media and communication (`media-communication`): Journalism, mass media and social communication.
- Natural sciences (`natural-sciences`): The sciences of nature and of formal systems, following OECD Fields of Science group 1: mathematics, computer science, physics, astronomy, chemistry, earth and life sciences.
  - Mathematics (`mathematics`): Number, quantity, structure, space and change.
  - Computer science (`computer-science`): Computation, algorithms, software and information.
  - Physics (`physics`): Matter, energy, forces and their laws.
  - Astronomy (`astronomy`): Celestial bodies and the universe, including cosmology.
  - Chemistry (`chemistry`): The composition, structure and reactions of substances.
  - Earth sciences (`earth-sciences`): The planet Earth and its environment.
    - Geology (`geology`): Rocks, minerals and the history of the Earth.
    - Meteorology and climatology (`meteorology`): Weather and climate.
    - Environmental science (`environmental-science`): The natural environment and human impact on it.
  - Biology (`biology`): Living organisms and life processes.
    - Botany (`botany`): Plants.
    - Zoology (`zoology`): Animals.
    - Genetics (`genetics`): Genes, heredity and variation.
    - Ecology (`ecology`): Relations of organisms with each other and their environment.
- Engineering and technology (`engineering-technology`): The design and making of structures, machines, systems and materials, following OECD Fields of Science group 2.
  - Civil engineering (`civil-engineering`): Structures, construction, transport infrastructure.
  - Mechanical engineering (`mechanical-engineering`): Machines, engines and mechanical systems.
  - Electrical and electronic engineering (`electrical-engineering`): Electricity, electronics and telecommunications.
  - Information technology (`information-technology`): Computers, networks, the internet and software as technology in use.
  - Aerospace engineering (`aerospace-engineering`): Aircraft and spacecraft.
  - Biotechnology (`biotechnology`): Technology using living organisms, including genetic engineering.
- Medical and health sciences (`medical-health-sciences`): Human health and its care, following OECD Fields of Science group 3.
  - Medicine (`medicine`): The diagnosis, treatment and prevention of disease.
  - Nursing (`nursing`): The care of the sick.
  - Public health (`public-health`): The health of populations: epidemics, prevention, health systems.
  - Pharmacology (`pharmacology`): Drugs and their effects.
- Religion (`religion`): Religious traditions and their life, worship, persons and art as expressions of culture. Theology as an academic discipline belongs under Humanities.
  - Christianity (`christianity`): The Christian faith as lived: churches, worship, saints, religious life.
    - Liturgy (`liturgy`): The public worship of the Church: Mass, sacraments, the liturgical year, the Liturgy of the Hours.
    - Saints (`saints`): Saints, blesseds and venerable servants of God, and their lives.
    - Religious orders (`religious-orders`): Monastic orders, congregations and other forms of consecrated life.
    - Sacred art (`sacred-art`): Art made for worship and devotion, considered as religious expression.
    - Popes (`popes`): The Popes and the papacy.
    - Christian denominations (`christian-denominations`): Orthodox, Protestant and other Christian churches and communities.
  - The Bible (`bible`): The books of Sacred Scripture, their persons and stories as such.
  - Judaism (`judaism`): The Jewish religion and its traditions.
  - Islam (`islam`): The Islamic religion and its traditions.
  - Eastern religions (`eastern-religions`): Hinduism, Buddhism, Taoism, Confucianism, Shinto and other religions of Asia.
  - Traditional religions (`traditional-religions`): Indigenous and ancient religions, including the religions of Greece and Rome.
  - New religious movements (`new-religious-movements`): Recent religious movements, esotericism and New Age.
- Popular culture (`popular-culture`): Everyday mass culture that is not itself an art form: sport, fashion, games and toys, fandom, internet culture.
  - Sport (`sport`): Sports, athletes and competitions.
  - Fashion (`fashion`): Clothing, style and the fashion industry.
  - Toys and games (`toys-games`): Toys, board and card games and other non-digital games.
  - Fandom (`fandom`): Fan communities and their creative practices.
  - Internet culture (`internet-culture`): Memes, online communities, influencers and social media phenomena.

### Gospel themes

- Theological virtues (`theological-virtues`): The virtues given by God that unite us to him: faith, hope and charity (CCC 1812–1829).
  - Faith (`faith`): Believing God and all he has revealed; trust and fidelity in him, doubt and the search for faith.
  - Hope (`hope`): Desiring eternal life and trusting in God's promises against despair.
  - Charity (`charity`): Love of God above all and of neighbour as oneself; self-giving love, love of enemies.
- Cardinal virtues (`cardinal-virtues`): The human virtues on which moral life hinges: prudence, justice, fortitude, temperance (CCC 1805–1809).
  - Prudence (`prudence`): Practical wisdom: discerning the true good and the right means.
  - Justice (`justice`): Giving God and neighbour their due; fairness, rights, the struggle against injustice.
  - Fortitude (`fortitude`): Courage and constancy in doing good, facing fear, trial and persecution.
  - Temperance (`temperance`): Mastery of desires and appetites; chastity, sobriety, self-control.
- Sin, grace and salvation (`sin-grace-salvation`): The drama of sin and of God's saving grace: fall, temptation, conversion, forgiveness, redemption.
  - Sin (`sin`): Evil chosen against God and neighbour, its roots and consequences.
  - Temptation (`temptation`): Enticement to evil and the struggle to resist it.
  - Repentance (`repentance`): Sorrow for sin and the resolve to amend one's life.
  - Conversion (`conversion`): Turning one's whole life back to God; a change of heart.
  - Forgiveness (`forgiveness`): Pardoning others and being pardoned; reconciliation after offence.
  - Mercy (`mercy`): Compassion that goes beyond justice, God's and ours; works of mercy.
  - Redemption (`redemption`): Being bought back from sin and death; a life redeemed.
  - Grace (`grace`): God's free and undeserved gift that heals and sanctifies.
  - Sacrifice (`sacrifice`): Giving one's life or goods for others or for God; self-sacrificial love.
- The human person (`human-person`): The dignity and destiny of the human being created in God's image (CCC 1700–1876).
  - Conscience (`conscience`): The inner voice judging good and evil; its formation and fidelity to it.
  - Freedom (`freedom`): Free will, responsibility and true freedom for the good.
  - Human dignity (`human-dignity`): The worth of every person from conception to natural death.
  - Suffering (`suffering`): Pain, illness, loss and the meaning of suffering.
  - Death (`death`): Mortality, dying and facing death.
  - Eternal life (`eternal-life`): The last things: judgment, heaven, hell, purgatory, the resurrection of the body.
  - Vocation (`vocation`): God's call to each person and its discernment.
- Communion and society (`communion-society`): Life with others: family, marriage, friendship, community, work, peace and creation.
  - Family (`family`): Parents and children, family bonds and their trials.
  - Marriage (`marriage`): The covenant of man and woman, fidelity and conjugal love.
  - Friendship (`friendship`): Bonds of friendship, loyalty and companionship.
  - Community (`community`): Belonging, solidarity and the common good of a group or people.
  - Work (`work`): Human labour, its dignity and its meaning.
  - Peace (`peace`): Peace and war, violence and nonviolence, reconciliation between peoples.
  - Care for creation (`creation`): Nature as God's gift and the human responsibility for it.
- Christ and the Church (`christ-church`): The mysteries of Christ and the life of the Church as they appear in a work.
  - Incarnation (`incarnation`): God made man; Christmas and the hidden life of Jesus.
  - The Cross (`cross`): The Passion and death of Christ; carrying one's cross.
  - Resurrection (`resurrection`): The Resurrection of Christ and new life over death.
  - Eucharist (`eucharist`): The Mass, Holy Communion and Eucharistic devotion.
  - Mary (`mary`): The Virgin Mary, Mother of God, and Marian devotion.
  - Holiness (`holiness`): The call to be holy; the witness of saints and martyrs.
  - Prayer (`prayer`): Speaking with God; prayer, contemplation and worship.
